description:
Tailscode is the native Mac window for every coding agent running on your own machines. Claude Code, opencode and Oh My Pi, on any model they can run, including one on your own graphics card: start them, watch six at once, steer them and read what they did, while each repository stays on the machine that owns it. Your chats go point to point over your own Tailscale network, never through a relay, with no sign-in. Free and open source.

ONE COMMAND TO SET UP
For Claude Code, one line on the computer you code on installs the bridge and ends with a pairing link. Paste it, confirm, and Tailscode has your machine; opencode has a one-line installer too. Want to look first? A built-in demo shows the main screens with no server at all.

EVERY AGENT AT A GLANCE
• The Agents window follows up to six running agents across your machines: the step each one is on, the command it is running or the file it is editing, with approve, answer, nudge and stop, and an inspector that peeks at any of them.
• The sidebar puts who needs you first, then what is working, pinned, saved and recent.
• Split the window into panes and put a different machine, project or conversation in each.

ANY MODEL, EVEN YOUR OWN GPU
• Whatever your agent can run, from cloud models to a local model served by Ollama or llama.cpp on your own machine, picked per chat with its reasoning effort.
• Carry a conversation to another model: the next one gets a short brief of the chat and picks up the thread.
• A party of six favourite models and their effort levels, one click or one chord away.

A LIVE, NATIVE TRANSCRIPT
• Streaming text, with thinking and tool runs folded into one readable trace per turn.
• Syntax-highlighted code with copy, and a diff for every Edit or Write the agent makes.
• Approvals, agent questions as answerable cards, and subagents in the same conversation.
• Queue a follow-up while the agent works, edit it before it lands, or stop the turn on the server.
• In Claude Code chats, the repository, read-only on purpose: branch, upstream drift, staged and changed files, and the diff behind each one.

ASK FROM ANYWHERE
• One global hotkey opens the ask box over any app and sends the question to the machine you choose.
• Not only code: ask what is eating the GPU, research a question, tidy a folder.
• Notifications when a turn needs you or finishes.

KEYBOARD FIRST
One shortcut registry, a vim-mode composer, a cheat sheet, a searchable command list, and a type size for each part of the window.

WHERE THE MONEY WENT
• Every conversation priced turn by turn, every month totalled across machines, by model, project and tool. Always an estimate, never a bill.
• Plan limits and quotas per provider and account.

YOURS, END TO END
• Your chats travel point to point over your tailnet, never through a relay. No sign-in, no ads, no tracking, and your code and conversations never reach us.
• Native AppKit, Swift 6, Liquid Glass, real menus, VoiceOver labels.
• Open source under GPL-3.0: the app, the engine and the bridges. Also on iPhone, iPad and Linux.

FREE, WITH AN HONEST PRO
Every screen but the delegate board is in the free app, on one server, for good. Tailscode Pro is a one-time purchase, no subscription: unlimited servers in one list, iPhone and Mac on the same Apple Account, the delegate board, and a supporter heart.

REQUIREMENTS
A computer on your Tailscale network (free for personal use) running opencode, Claude Code through claude-bridge, or Oh My Pi through omp-bridge. Tailscode is independent open-source software, not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic, Tailscale Inc., the opencode project or Oh My Pi.

Privacy policy: https://midgarcorp.cc/tailscode/privacy
Source code: https://github.com/guitaripod/Tailscode
promotionalText: Run Claude Code, opencode and Oh My Pi on your own computers, on any model they can run, even your own GPU, and watch them all from one native window. No sign-in.
whatsNew:
New:
• Agents window and wall. What needs you, with the answer in place, what is working, what runs in the background and what finished in the last hour, with a peek inspector and an hour of lanes. The window opens on the wall: every agent on a Metal ground, laid out for any window size, with hold to approve. Show Agents in the menu or the sidebar opens it.
• Carry a conversation to another model: continue on another machine with a short brief, or branch a chat from any answer with Try with another model.
• A party of six models, from the model pill and in Quick ask.
• Meet Megatron: one head per turn, a line while it works and a stage with the Metal head, numbered steps, pinning, replay and a Share poster. Choose Megatron or Lines in Settings.
• Meridian, a world clock beside the update mark, with pinned places, quota windows, alarms and copy as ISO, UTC or epoch.
• Talk to the agent, in beta: a call strip above the composer listens and types into the chat.
• Restart one server, or every server at once, from the app.
• The usage share is modular: a format for X, a square or a portrait, with the modules you choose.
• First run is one checklist: the machine on your tailnet, a pairing link, claude-bridge installed and proof that it answers.
• The picture and video studios list every missing ComfyUI model and node with a copy-the-command row, and the gallery is a wide grid with save, share, copy and paint again.
• Quotas are one card per provider and account.

Changes:
• The page scrolls past an open Megatron, and long chats open with less main-thread work.
• Where the server keeps a queue, queued messages wait there, and edit, cancel and resume go to the server.
• The App Store build finds your Tailscale machines, with the token kept in the Keychain.
• Game Center sign-in is opt-in.

Fixes:
• The quick-ask hotkey no longer crashes the app.
• Crashes in AppKit callbacks on macOS 27.2 are fixed.
• Saving a Tailscale token starts the scan.
• A Full Disk Access row opens System Settings even when the server's request fails.
• Megatron's account no longer crashes after an open turn, and the Studio's picture buttons answer the pointer.
• An open chat keeps the model and effort the server has.
• The chat follows the Mac between light and dark.
• The Agents entry in the sidebar no longer squeezes the chat list.
• The status line holds still, and a failed quota read keeps the last good numbers.
• opencode 2 conversations get their names.
